tools.name: artifact.certify
tools.description: Certifies a Forge NormalizedVizSpec IR, optionally with the chart's DATA. Returns a per-pillar verdict summary (a11yEquivalence, determinism, contrast, accuracy — five-valued on contrast, four-valued on accuracy) that disaggregates what was actually checked, plus — on the cartesian path only — a folded conformance verdict (light theme). Cartesian CONTRAST is render-measured (s176): certify renders the compiled spec through @oods/viz-render and grades the series-to-paint assignment the data marks actually carry, duplicates retained, so a recycled palette (more consumed series than baked hexes) truthfully fails as a ΔE00=0 pair; ECharts contrast is render-measured when `data` is supplied: actual chart carriers feed Role C and the semantic N-long assignment feeds Role A; geo families remain exempt while retaining render evidence. spec-only calls retain the reconstructed baked-palette verdict. Data-backed ECharts determinism retains contentHash as projected-option identity and adds renderHash for the first normalized SVG when rendering succeeds; a second independent option emission and render prove `stable`. A typed first-render fault omits renderHash and makes stable false, while bubble_map without inline geometry keeps the option proof and names the limitation. The runtime contract and render-hash epoch are pinned in packages/viz-render/certified-matrix.json. The folded verdict folds the graded pillars: 'fail' OR 'ungradeable' on contrast or accuracy pulls conformant false — ungradeable (s175) means grading was ATTEMPTED and failed for a reason outside the spec (an unresolvable canvas token, an evaluator fault); 'unchecked' (nothing to grade) and 'exempt' leave it a11y-driven. contrast and accuracy enums now carry 'ungradeable'; an exhaustive switch must handle it. Read-only: reads the IR and the operand, never rebuilds or re-recommends. The 8 ECharts-primary types return coverage:'uncertified'/conformant:null — a distinct verdict, not a failure, and NOT a statement that nothing was checked: contrast has carried a real verdict for them since s141, and as of s172 DETERMINISM and ACCURACY do too whenever the caller supplies the optional `data` operand (the same data branch viz.render takes; exactly one branch, matching the mark trait). With it, certify re-emits the ECharts option twice and its contentHash equals viz.render's for the SAME (spec, data) pair, and it evaluates a per-type accuracy set (OODS-V154..V159); without it those two pillars stay 'unchecked' and notes[] names the missing operand. `data` on a cartesian spec is a structured error — dead input, not a silent no-op. Read accuracy:'pass' precisely: none of the rules OFFERED for that chart type positively detected its distortion, with accuracySummary.rulesEvaluated reporting how many actually ran; it is not a claim that the chart is accurate. a11y-equivalence runs WARN-FIRST for these 8 whenever the operand is supplied: the 16 rules evaluate over the operand-built table and narrative, each reporting pass, fail, or not-applicable with its absent precondition named; failures surface in findings[] as OODS-A11Y-<rule.id> at their native severity, and not-applicable rules surface in the top-level a11yNotApplicable[] channel as {rule, preconditionAbsent} — present exactly when the engine ran on the data-backed path, absent on a {spec}-only call. pillars.a11yEquivalence deliberately stays 'unchecked' — warn-first moves no verdict; the flip to pass/fail is a future enforce step. Without the operand no a11y rule runs. IF YOUR CLIENT CACHES THIS TEXT (s173 m01): tool EXECUTION is read fresh from the built server on every call, so a Forge update reaches your results immediately — but this description and the input schema are what your connector advertised AT CONNECT TIME, so after a Forge release you are reading the old contract until you RECONNECT.

tools.name: dashboard.render
tools.description: Renders a composed metric-overview dashboard (KPI row + trend + breakdown + optional geo) from a declarative DashboardSpec; composes per-panel viz specs in-process with deterministic layout, KPI compute, and cross-filtering. Returns the resolved layout + per-panel specs + a synthesized a11y block and a specRef for pipeline reuse.
